statement: Let $ABCD$ be a trapezoid with $AB \parallel CD$, $|AB| > |CD|$, and $|AD| = |BC|$. Let $I$ be the centre of the circle tangent to lines $AB$, $AC$, and $BD$, where $A$ and $I$ are on opposite sides of $BD$. Let $J$ be the centre of the circle tangent to lines $CD$, $AC$, and $BD$, where $D$ and $J$ are on opposite sides of $AC$. Prove that $|IC| = |JB|$.

Let $n \geq 2$ be a fixed positive integer and suppose that $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$ are positive real numbers satisfying $a_1 + a_2 + \cdots + a_n = 2^n - 1$. Find the minimum possible value of
$$\frac{a_1}{1} + \frac{a_2}{1 + a_1} + \frac{a_3}{1 + a_1 + a_2} + \cdots + \frac{a_n}{1 + a_1 + a_2 + \cdots + a_{n-1}}.$$

At a dinner party there are $N$ hosts and $N$ guests ($N \geq 4$) seated around a circular table. Two guests will chat if either at most one person sits between them, or exactly two people sit between them with at least one being a host. Prove that no matter how the $2N$ people are seated, at least $N$ pairs of guests will chat.

A function $f$ from the positive integers to the positive integers is called Canadian if it satisfies
$$\gcd(f(f(x)),\, f(x+y)) = \gcd(x, y)$$
for all pairs of positive integers $x$ and $y$. Find all positive integers $m$ such that $f(m) = m$ for all Canadian functions $f$.

Nina and Tadashi play the following game. Initially a triple $(a, b, c)$ of nonnegative integers with $a + b + c = 2021$ is written on a blackboard. They take turns (Nina first); a player chooses a positive integer $k$ and one of the three entries, increases it by $k$, and decreases the other two by $k$. A player loses if on their turn some entry becomes negative. Find the number of initial triples $(a, b, c)$ for which Tadashi has a winning strategy.
